authorisation: D82, the Product Owner's continuation of the mission of 2026-10-29 (a defect found while deploying Central least privilege).
implementation: The retention sweep (stayconnect-backup-cleanup.sh) ordered config backups by modification time. A backup made with cp -a or cp -p keeps its source's modification time, so copies of an unchanged file tie and the newest-named copy was swept first. Found on Central on 2026-10-29: the sweep removed the env-file backup that the least-privilege deploy had just made (the deploy reported it kept). retain_group now orders by change time (ls -t -c). The self-test lifts the function out of the script and proves that, of five copies tied on modification time, the newest three are kept.
verification: stayconnect-backup-cleanup-selftest.sh on Linux: every case passes, including the new one. The defect was observed live on Central before the fix.
deployment: At the time of this receipt: NOT deployed. The sweep is part of both releases; the deployment follows the merge and is recorded by its own receipt.
